craft_notes: Sthāyin: the definition — scripture as vimarśana. Sanskrit-first: triple locative stack (universe/consciousness/sound-nature) kept climbing; yat…tat eva kept the equational frame; bhāge bhāge rūḍhi kept part-by-part (pedagogical grading, not ontological). Rows: 2 (long compound ekādhikāryuddeśenaiva unpacked by enjambment), 9 (world-thing/act-fruit pair), 1 ('stands part by part' closes — rūḍhi end-weight), 12 (equation settles). Close: 'people's establishment stands part by part.' Rejected: summarizing the locative stack — killed: the climb IS the definition; 'scriptures' for the single śāstram — killed: singular verdict kept.

lines: Therein — the universe made of mere consciousness,
and consciousness of vimarśa-nature, and vimarśa's
whatever contemplation that is — that is scripture.
Whole scripture, in fact, is one-fruit-attaining
people's establishment stands part by part.
l4.sanskrit_cite: tatra saṃvinmātramaye viśvasmin saṃvidi ca vimarśātmikāyāṃ vimarśasya ca śabdanātmakatāyāṃ siddhāyāṃ sakalajaganniṣṭhavastunaḥ tadgatasya ca karmaphalasambandhavaicitryasya yat vimarśanaṃ tad eva śāstram iti parameśvarasvabhāvābhinna eva samastaḥ śāstrasaṃdarbho vastuta ekaphalaprāpakaḥ ekādhikāryuddeśenaiva tatra tu parameśvaraniyatiśaktimahimnaiva bhāge bhāge rūḍhiḥ lokānām iti

reads_against.argmap: What makes something scripture? → Śāstra is defined as vimarśana of the established world: structurally one-fruit, pedagogically part-graded by the Lord's necessity-power.
c1_essence: Scripture is vimarśana of the world-thing in the consciousness-made universe — one-fruit in structure, part-graded in rūḍhi by the Lord's necessity-power.
reads_against.c1_rasa: adbhuta-śānta of authority established (wonder settling into doctrinal calm)
